source_text: Quam commixtionem ita exsecrabilem persuadere conatus es, ut velis intellegi Christum, non propter signi splendorem, sed propter damnandam sexuum coniunctionem nasci de virgine matre voluisse. Quid ergo umquam a quoquam dici improbius aut impudentius potuit, quam hoc, quod duos velut reges de humanitatis possessione certantes his signis, et duo eorum regna separasti, ut diceres, dia li esse quidquid nuptiae protulissent, Dei vero solum quod Virgo peperisset? Quid est aliud, Virginis fecundatorem et egentissimum ostendere inopia portionis suae, et eumdem negare eorum qui prodeunt de nuptiis hominum conditorem? Teneat igitur verbi tui lector diligens chirographum, sciatque te, discipulum fidelem Manichaeorum et Traducianae nationis primatem, nihil aliud quam commixtionem legitimi damnasse coniugii.
pass_a_gloss: Which mingling you tried to persuade so execrable, that you want it understood that Christ willed to be born from a virgin mother not on account of the brightness of the sign, but on account of a union of the sexes to be condemned. What therefore could ever have been said by anyone more wicked or more shameless than this, that you, as if two kings fighting about the possession of humanity, by these signs, also separated two kingdoms of them, so that you would say that whatever marriages had brought forth is the devil's, but of God only what the Virgin had borne? What else is it, to show the fecundator of the Virgin even most needy by the want of his own portion, and to deny the same to be the founder of those humans who come forth from marriages? Let therefore a diligent reader of your word hold the handwritten acknowledgment, and know that you, a faithful disciple of the Manichaeans and primate of the Traducian nation, have condemned nothing other than the mingling of a lawful marriage.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: You tried to make this union seem so accursed that you would have us understand that Christ chose to be born of a virgin mother, not for the splendor of the sign, but to condemn the union of the sexes (compare Matthew 1:18–23; Luke 1:34–35). What could anyone ever have said more wickedly or shamelessly than this? You distinguished two apparent kings contending for the possession of humanity, and their two kingdoms, by saying that whatever marriage produced belonged to the devil, while only what the Virgin bore belonged to God. What else does this do but represent the one who made the Virgin fruitful as utterly impoverished by the smallness of his share, and deny that he is the Creator of human beings who come from marriage? Let the careful reader retain the written acknowledgment supplied by your own words, then, and know that you, a faithful disciple of the Manichaeans and leader of the advocates of inherited sin, have condemned nothing other than the union of lawful marriage (Matthew 1:18–23) (Luke 1:34–35) (Matthew 1:18–23; Luke 1:34–35).

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)
